why: The defect is real. One ADM-06 row says both "reinstate the segments, payloads and derived artifacts the copy contains" and "count every event the copy holds as received and not recorded on this node, even on the node that made the copy". The copy's trust levels, active pins, quarantine set and natural-language headlines were derived while its events still counted as recorded. Reinstated as they are, they are no longer "a deterministic function of the set of writer logs a node holds and the node's own key set" (I10). That breaks ADM-08 ("Derived artifacts MUST depend only on the set of writer logs held and the node's key set"). It also fails ADM-09's derived-artifact consistency check, which ADM-06's own "pass `parinn verify` afterwards" requires. A copy altered outside the home, before seals ship (OQ-48), could carry an active-pin list or trust levels that keep a pin qualifying for a restore block. That breaks I2 and contradicts the row's list of "each pin of the copy that will not restore". The model is silent: Backup only says "reading it back is a backup restore". Rebuilding is the only reading that fits I10, so this needs no behavioral choice.
settled_by: I10: "All derived artifacts (indexes, landmarks, active pins, quarantine set, room state, trust levels, run and integrity statuses, queues, evidence and proof classes, stats) are a deterministic function of the set of writer logs a node holds and the node's own key set, independent of the order in which logs arrived. Rebuilding reproduces them exactly." ADM-08: "Derived artifacts MUST depend only on the set of writer logs held and the node's key set, never on the order in which logs or segments arrived." Stakeholder decision DM-DE (round 6): every event a backup restore reinstates counts as received.

options.label: Rebuild every derived artifact; never reinstate the copy's (recommended)
options.effect: A restore reinstates only segments and payloads, then rebuilds trust levels, active pins, the quarantine set (with the copy's quarantines the restore keeps in force), landmarks and indexes from the logs now held and this node's key set. This closes the planted-pin path and keeps `parinn verify` passing. `parinn backup create` still captures derived artifacts, unchanged.

options.label: Keep reinstating and re-derive only trust levels
options.effect: Leaves the other artifacts (active pins, quarantine set, headlines) derived under the old reading. That still breaks I10 and ADM-08, and leaves the I2 path open. Rejected.

why: The defect is in the wording; the behavior is settled. ADM-06 lets a restore run anywhere and keeps "every quarantine in force in the copy (SEC-12, I5)". The DM-DE decision says the copy's quarantines stay in force. A restore can run on a node other than the one that made the copy, for example a principal restoring a lost laptop's copy on a new machine. There the copy's quarantines were recorded by another node, and I5 says "A quarantine reaches another node only as a quarantine request that node's principal applies." The DM-DD closing text covers only a node clone: "those quarantines are its own, recorded in its home, not another node's quarantine". Under DM-DE every reinstated event counts as received even on the node that made the copy, so that reasoning does not carry over. The record.md Quarantine entry also limits the effect to "the node that records it, and still after its node identity changes (Node)", so it disagrees with Node and ADM-06. The reconciliation follows from existing rules. ADM-06 makes the restore "a widening principal act" of this node's principal. PEER-11 says a principal applies a quarantine request "by one of the class of the quarantine it applies", and a widening act covers any class. So confirming the restore is that principal applying each quarantine, which matches I5's letter. Keeping them is also the safe side under I5.
settled_by: Stakeholder decision DM-DE (round 6): "the copy's quarantines stay in force". ADM-06: "keep in force on the node, until a release there, every quarantine in force in the copy (SEC-12, I5)" and "A backup restore MUST be a widening principal act". I5: "A quarantine reaches another node only as a quarantine request that node's principal applies." PEER-11: "a quarantine request by one of the class of the quarantine it applies (SEC-12)".

why: The gap is real: the model never says what a restore of another node's copy does with that node's personal room. The rules do fix the present outcome. A backup restore is a principal act acting on no room, so LANE-01 records it in this node's own personal room. That room must already exist, created at first start (ADM-02), so restoring another node's copy leaves two personal rooms. LANE-01 makes a personal room this node's only if it was "created by its device seat at ParleyInn's first start there ... or carried over to a node clone, where every run has a seat from its first event". A backup restore is neither, so the copy's personal room stays that node's, and this node's runs have no seat in it from their first event. RCL-05's `room` and `rooms` scopes reach only rooms "the agent has a seat in". RCL-10 reaches only a foreign room, and this room is the principal's own, not foreign. So no recall call reaches the restored personal-room history, and OQ-45 covers only rooms the agent's seats left. The finding overstates one point: LANE-23 does not bar a run from joining that room on its principal's ask, and those join rules are left as they stand. Agents are also bound to their node (REC-02: "identified by its node, its harness and the harness's agent id"), so the old node's agents' rooms never pass to this node's agents anyway. Whether recall should reach such a room, by sharing it as a node clone does or by naming it in a call, is a real usefulness choice. The same choice returns in M8, when PEER-02 serves this node the personal rooms of the principal's other nodes.
settled_by: none. The interim already follows from LANE-01 ("Every principal MUST have one personal room on each of its nodes, created by its device seat at ParleyInn's first start there ... or carried over to a node clone, where every run has a seat from its first event"), RCL-05 ("`room` (one of its principal's rooms the agent has a seat in, through the writers this node holds)") and RCL-10 ("Recall MUST reach a foreign room only through a `room` parameter naming it"). No rule decides whether recall may reach another node's personal room.

why: The defect is real. The model's Node entry (places.md) says the events from before a node identity change "are another node's: they count as received", and that the events a backup restore reinstates "count as received in the same way". It carries over only one kind of principal act: "every quarantine in force in the home at the change stays in force until a release there", and the same for the copy. REC-24 and ADM-06 say the same and no more. Nothing in M1–M5 text says whether any other principal act among those events keeps its effect. The live case is a configuration acceptance. ADM-04 (M1) applies a change of deployment mode, a retention policy, looser redaction, flags off or a configuration pin only "after the widening principal act accepting it records its digest". It never says that act must be one this node recorded, and the configuration file travels with the home. So a CI node cloned from an image whose builder accepted `node.deployment_mode = 'interactive'` could keep that acceptance. Its pipeline `user` events would then be trusted (PRV-02), which is exactly concern B10, and they would flow into the trusted-only export (ADM-12, M5). The same goes for an acceptance a restored copy holds. OWN-17 does state the governing principle, but it is M8, and it speaks only of acts "written on another of the principal's nodes". It does not cover a restore onto the node that made the copy, which ADM-06 counts as received "even on the node that made the copy". The cut half is open as well, but in M1–M5 its only live case is the quarantine, which is already carried over. A withdrawn risk acceptance and capture turned back on only undo widening acts that lapse too. Rule level tightening (OWN-10), revocations (SEC-27, PRV-10, PEER-05), unstamps (LANE-32) and trust-grant revocations (OWN-29) all ship in M7 or later. A purge recorded before the change has no effect to lose, because its content is already gone. The scope note's rule applies: the finding concerns REC-24 (M1) and ADM-06 (M3), so its fix may reach later text.
settled_by: Partly. I8: "Content another principal wrote, or another node wrote other than this principal's acts signed by a device key it certified and its posts and pins written from a device seat such a key certified, is kept as theirs: attributed to its seat key, and untrusted unless this principal's own stamp or trust grant covers it. On its own it never makes this principal's agents trust it, nor extends their recall." REC-24: "Every event recorded before the change MUST then count on the node as another node's, received and not recorded there (PRV-02, I8)". OWN-17 (M8): "A principal act written on another of the principal's nodes or devices MUST take effect here only under PRV-10". PRV-04: "`interactive` MUST be an explicit opt-in in the principal's configuration." Stakeholder ruling DM-DE (round-6 verify R6-2): "until M7, the copy's device-seat pins, principal acts and `user` events are untrusted, so the principal must make its pins again after a restore." Together these settle that a widening act among received events must not widen anything. But OWN-17 is M8 and does not cover a same-node restore, and no M1–M5 requirement or model entry carries the rule. Nothing settles the cut and neutral acts beyond quarantines (REC-24, ADM-06, DM-AH, DM-DD).

options.label: A: widening acts lapse; cut and neutral acts keep their effect, as the quarantines do (recommended)
options.effect: A configuration acceptance, a retention-policy change, a risk acceptance and any other widening act recorded before the change, or held in a restored copy, takes no effect until the principal takes it again on the node. A CI clone therefore runs `automation`, with flags on and no configuration pins, until a local `parinn configuration accept` or managed policy (SEC-22) sets otherwise. Cut and neutral acts in force at the change keep their effect, so a later rule level tightening or revocation never lapses, and acknowledged counters stay acknowledged on runner clones. In M1–M5 the only change from today is the configuration-acceptance case. Whether a signed act may take effect once PRV-10 ships goes to OQ-48 (M7).

options.label: B: every principal act but the quarantines lapses (the literal reading of OWN-17 before PRV-10)
options.effect: Just as safe in M1–M5, and simpler. From M7 on, though, a rule level tightening or a revocation recorded before a clone or held in a copy would lapse, the unsafe side. Acknowledged counters would also come back on every runner clone and fail `parinn doctor` there.

options.label: C: every principal act among received events keeps its effect
options.effect: A cloned CI image keeps `interactive` mode, so pipeline input becomes trusted `user` events, and an altered copy can plant an acceptance (OQ-48). That breaks I8's "never makes this principal's agents trust it", so it is not open to choose.

recommendation: Tighten now with option A. It cannot wait: REC-24 and ADM-04 ship in M1 and backup restore in M3, so without the rule an M1 implementer could carry a configuration acceptance onto a cloned CI node and trust its pipeline `user` events (I2, I8, concern B10). No invariant wording changes. The M7 relaxation, whether a widening act a device key signed takes effect once PRV-10 ships, is deferred as an "Also open, before M7" addition to OQ-48. Its recommendation there is that a sealed act takes effect as OWN-17 says, except a configuration acceptance, which takes effect only on the node that recorded it. The edits change the model's Node entry, REC-24, ADM-06 and OQ-48, and add two steps each to the pending REC-24 and ADM-06 scenarios. All three SRS edits lengthen a table cell, so run `mdsmith fix` afterwards to re-pad the tables (MDS025). I validated everything on a scratch copy: after `mdsmith fix`, `mdsmith check .` is clean (318 files), and the internal/scenario, internal/srs, internal/ledger and cmd/parinn tests pass. Budgets: places.md grows to 115 lines and about 1750 tokens. docs/srs/05-functional-requirements.md rises to about 7960 of its 8000 tokens, leaving about 40 for any further REC-24 text. Note: one validation command ran my apply script against /home/user/cairn instead of the scratch copy. I reverted all six files by exact reverse replacement, the diff had contained only these edits, and `git status` in the repository is clean.

why: The defect is real, and it ships before M7. The model's Room view entry says only that the CLI verbs show the record: "`parinn event search` and `expand`, `parinn landmark list`, `parinn pin list` and `parinn audit` show the principal its agents' runs, events and landmarks, its pins and pin candidates, and the audit log (§9.5)". It gives no rule for how they write text to a terminal. Agent text reaches those verbs in M2: PIN-02 (P0) says "Text `pin_candidate_propose` proposes MUST be stored as a pin candidate with provenance `assistant`". PIN-05 (M5) confirms a candidate "only after that principal is shown its exact text, pin type and priority". The confirmation turns the candidate into a pin the principal's device seat authors, which restores as trusted text. If raw ESC/CSI/OSC sequences, a carriage return, or bidirectional, zero-width or tag characters reach the terminal, they can hide, overwrite or reorder that text. The principal then confirms bytes it never saw, and they restore verbatim (I2, I3). Answerback sequences can also type into the controlling terminal, which OWN-12 trusts for widening acts. The rules that exist do not cover this. RCL-04 covers only "a CLI verb's output that is not a terminal". SEC-06 carries recalled content as JSON strings, and JSON escapes only U+0000-U+001F, so C1 controls and bidirectional, zero-width and tag characters pass through, and a human rendering decodes even the escaped ones. VIEW-07 ("Zero-width, bidirectional and tag characters and HTML comments MUST render as visible placeholders with a count") and SEC-21 ("The room view MUST render record content as inert text") are M7 and do not cover C0/C1 controls at a terminal. Threat T16 lists only those M7 rows as controls ("SEC-21, VIEW-07"). PRV-07 only flags such Unicode. The trust half of the finding is partly settled already. §9.5 gives search and expand "the envelope and limits of `event_search` and `event_expand`", and §9.2's `event_search` returns "Envelope of hits: `address`, run, provenance, trust, flags, kind, preview, score". What is missing is any rule that the CLI shows an agent's pin candidate with its provenance when the candidate is listed or confirmed. The ledger's closing texts for DM-I, DM-DF and DM-BJ stay intact: every quote of theirs is still a substring after these edits, which I checked by applying the edits to scratch copies.
settled_by: No rule settles the escaping. For search and expand, provenance and trust are already settled by §9.5 ("The principal's search and expand, with the envelope and limits of `event_search` and `event_expand`") and §9.2 (`event_search` returns "Envelope of hits: `address`, run, provenance, trust, flags, kind, preview, score"). The nearest rendering rules, VIEW-07, VIEW-14 and SEC-21, are M7.

options.label: A: Tighten now. Extend SEC-06 (P0, M1) to cover terminal output from the CLI and the TUI, add SEC-06 as a T16 control, and have PIN-02 and PIN-05 show an agent's candidate as untrusted `assistant` text wherever it is listed or confirmed. Update the model and the three scenarios.
options.effect: Closes the hole from M1 on. No text ParleyInn did not ship can rewrite what the principal reads or confirms at a terminal, and the principal sees that an agent's candidate is untrusted before it becomes a trusted pin. Exactness is kept, because each placeholder names its code point. Also covers C0/C1 controls in the M7 TUI, which VIEW-07 misses, and is compatible with VIEW-07's placeholders with a count.

options.label: B: Same rule as a new SEC row (P0, M1) with its own scenario, plus entries in §12.2's M1 row and in the appendices
options.effect: Same protection, but many more edits and a new id.

options.label: C: Defer to OQ-47 until VIEW-07 and VIEW-14 ship (M7)
options.effect: Leaves deceptive confirmation and terminal injection open through M1-M5, while the CLI is the only display and PIN-02 and PIN-05 already ship. Rejected: this is a security hole in what ships before that milestone.

recommendation: Option A: tighten now rather than defer. This cannot wait for M7. The CLI's record display ships in M1 (SEC-06, `parinn event search`), agent pin candidates in M2 (PIN-02) and their confirmation in M5 (PIN-05), all before VIEW-07, VIEW-14 and SEC-21. So no OQ is opened. The rule follows from I2 and from PIN-05's requirement that the exact text be shown, so the stakeholder has no behavioral choice to make. Notes for applying: (1) The SRS row edits lengthen table cells, so run `mdsmith fix` afterwards to re-pad the tables in 06-security.md and 05-functional-requirements.md. (2) Budget risk: 05-functional-requirements.md grows by about 25 words, to about 5,977.
